reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and consistent with that, no redline or comment was proposed — the rendered paragraphs are identical to the originals, so there is no invalid or directionally wrong edit to correct.

The cited text supports compliance: p0065 provides a 'renewable one-year term' with no automatic-renewal mechanic, no non-renewal notice window and no multi-year roll-over, so renewal is effectively by agreement — the rule's preferred position. p0117 makes the licence perpetual while fees are paid, and no unilateral vendor uplift/escalation right is present, so uncapped renewal repricing is unavailable.

The failed deterministic check (value=90) is a false positive: the 90-day period in p0118 is our own (Sparkling/Customer) termination-for-convenience notice right, not a non-renewal notice window imposed on us, and a customer-favourable right should not be flagged. It is also not longer than the 90-day walk-away threshold.

The noted gaps (no express CPI/3% cap, no 60-day vendor renewal reminder) are correctly treated as preferred-only sub-elements recorded in the rationale rather than redlined, per the classification semantics.
